delivery.outcome: Adopting repositories can install a pyqual-style worktree-guard.yaml that fail-closes undeclared overlapping writes across sibling worktrees, and a workspace can run the same check on a timer and on .worktrees changes
nonGoals: No rewrite of package-manifest.json or governance_check.py in this ticket
No change to the terminal workspace_lifecycle_check default
No JSON Schema file for worktree-guard.yaml in this ticket; deferred to stay inside the 9-file policy limit

architecture.decision: Publish a standalone overlap checker and YAML runner that adopters copy via install-worktree-guard.sh. Keep workspace_lifecycle_check.py terminal-only. Do not touch files owned by ticket-089/090/091. Amended 2026-08-19: emitting new GOV-* codes is not optional work — the repository's own validator fails with GOV-DIAGNOSTIC-001 on any code missing from governance/diagnostics.json, and ci.yml refuses to pass while a tests/*.test.sh exists that no step runs. Both files are therefore part of delivering this outcome, not adjacent scope. Budget raised 8 -> 10 for exactly those two files. The hub policy caps implementation files at 9, so the JSON Schema for worktree-guard.yaml is deferred to a dependent ticket: nothing references it, and the runner already rejects an unknown schema value at load time.
interfaceChanges: worktree-guard.yaml is a new adopted trigger file, like pyqual.yaml
architecture.rollback: Delete the new files; no managed package-manifest entry was added

validation.evidence: Synthetic fixture: shared app.py fails, disjoint paths pass, conflictsWith serialises, a stale ticket copy in a third worktree is not attributed, --identity-of narrows reporting without narrowing discovery, --report and --print-pyqual-stage emit the documented shapes, and the installer writes idempotent units.
44 checkouts, 8 findings, all naming real overlapping paths
Timer and path unit active for both workspace roots; the path unit was observed firing on a .worktrees change and the report file was rewritten
scope=remote:github.com/subactor/core, 7 findings, while the workspace scan of the same tree reports 11 across all identities

Hook installed into git rev-parse --git-path hooks for unset, tracked and non-standard core.hooksPath; an overlapping commit is refused with GOV-WORKTREE-OVERLAP-FAIL, a disjoint one is accepted, an unrelated repository's conflict does not block, and re-wiring does not duplicate the call. A poisoned GIT_DIR environment must not change the checkout count.

commands: bash -c 'for s in tests/*.test.sh; do grep -Fq "bash $s" .github/workflows/ci.yml || exit 1; done'
validation.evidence: The three GOV-WORKTREE-OVERLAP codes are registered in the diagnostics catalog, so the validator reports no GOV-DIAGNOSTIC-001, and the workflow's suite-list assertion passes.
